text.name: I have provided two UI color documentation references: 1. Brand Color Style Guide 2. Supporting Color Style Guide Please review and understand both documents completely before creating anything. OBJECTIVE Create a complete and properly structured Figma Color Variable System based strictly on the colors, names, HEX codes, shades, Q values, and usage defined in these two documents. IMPORTANT RULES 1. SOURCE OF TRUTH - The two provided color documents are the only source of truth. - Do not invent, modify, replace, or add any colors. - Use the exact HEX/RGB values provided in the documents. - Preserve the exact Q Value/Hue information defined in the documentation. - The Brand Blue hue value is 220 and must NEVER be changed. - Every swatch must use the exact documented color code. 2. PRIMITIVE VARIABLES Create all documented colors first as Primitive Variables. Organize the primitives clearly under: - Brand Colors - Brand Blue / Monochromatic - Supporting Colors - Gradient Colors - Other documented color groups For Brand Blue Monochromatic, create the complete documented 50–900 scale exactly as provided. Also include the documented: - Blue → White shades - Blue → Black shades - Blue → Grey shades - Brand Gradient - Supporting / Symmetric colors such as Success, Warning, Error, and Info Do not change any shade or HEX value. 3. VARIABLE NAMING Use a clean and consistent naming structure. Example: Brand / Base / Blue Brand / Base / White Brand / Base / Black Brand / Base / Grey Brand / Blue / 50 Brand / Blue / 100 Brand / Blue / 200 ... Brand / Blue / 900 Brand / Blue-White / [documented scale] Brand / Blue-Black / [documented scale] Brand / Blue-Grey / [documented scale] Supporting / Success Supporting / Warning Supporting / Error Supporting / Info Use the actual documented names from the provided files wherever applicable. 4. SEMANTIC TOKENS After creating all Primitive Variables, create a separate Semantic Token collection. Do not duplicate color values in Semantic Tokens. Semantic Tokens must reference/alias the Primitive Variables. Create two major groups: SET 01 — COLOR / SURFACE TOKENS This set should contain the general color application tokens, including: - Brand / Base Colors - Brand / Blue Monochromatic - Blue / White - Blue / Black - Blue / Grey - Brand Gradients - Supporting / Success - Supporting / Warning - Supporting / Error - Supporting / Info These should be available as semantic aliases and should ultimately reference the correct Primitive Variables. SET 02 — UI USAGE TOKENS Create semantic tokens for actual UI usage: TEXT - Text / Primary - Text / Secondary - Text / Tertiary - Text / White - Text / Black - Text / Grey - Add other text levels only if they are defined in the documentation. BACKGROUND Create the documented background levels, such as: - Background / Primary - Background / Secondary - Background / Tertiary - Background / [additional documented levels] BORDER - Border / Primary - Border / Secondary - Border / [additional documented levels] ICON - Icon / Primary - Icon / Secondary - Icon / Tertiary - Icon / [additional documented levels] ACTION Create the documented action color tokens. BUTTON Create button color tokens with the documented variations: - Button / Primary - Button / Secondary - Button / Success - Other documented button states/variations For each button variation, support both: - Solid color - Gradient The Primary button must use the documented Brand Blue color. Use the exact documented HEX value and gradient definition. FEEDBACK Create: - Feedback / Success - Feedback / Warning - Feedback / Error - Feedback / Info 5. GRADIENTS Create gradient variables only from the gradients documented in the Brand Color document. Do not create new gradients. For the Primary Button Gradient: - Use the exact documented Brand Primary Linear Gradient. - Preserve the exact start color, end color, direction, and values from the documentation. 6. VARIABLE COLLECTION STRUCTURE Keep Primitive Variables and Semantic Tokens clearly separated. Do not mix primitive values with semantic aliases. Recommended structure: PRIMITIVES - Brand Colors - Brand Blue / Monochromatic - Blue / White - Blue / Black - Blue / Grey - Supporting Colors - Gradients SEMANTIC TOKENS - Color / Base - Color / Text - Color / Background - Color / Border - Color / Icon - Color / Action - Color / Button - Color / Feedback 7. ACCURACY CHECK Before finishing: - Compare every created variable against the provided documents. - Verify every HEX code. - Verify every shade from 50–900. - Verify the Q Value. - Verify the Brand Blue hue value of 220. - Verify all gradients. - Verify all Success, Warning, Error, and Info colors. - Ensure there are no missing documented colors. - Ensure there are no invented colors. - Ensure semantic tokens correctly alias the corresponding primitive variables. 8. DO NOT CHANGE THE DESIGN DOCUMENT Do not modify existing UI screens or components unless explicitly required. The task is only to create and organize the Color Variable System. The final result should be clean, scalable, developer-friendly, and ready to be used as the official UI Design System color foundation.
Semantic colour tokens — how colours are applied across the interface. Each token aliases a primitive colour for consistent, theme-ready usage.
Core identity aliases — Brand Blue, White, Black, and Grey mapped from Primitives.
Primary gradient colour stops for branded gradient fills.
Full brand blue scale for consistent tonal variation across the UI.
Light tonal scale aliases for subtle background and surface variations.
Dark tonal scale aliases for dark mode surfaces and high-contrast text.
Neutral scale aliases for UI surfaces, borders, and secondary text.
Semantic text colours — primary, secondary, tertiary, and special purpose text fills.
Surface colours for page backgrounds and content areas.
Border and divider colours for structural separation.
Icon fill colours across emphasis levels.
Interactive action colours — primary, hover, active, and disabled states.
Button fill and text colours for all button variants.
Success status scale for positive feedback and confirmations.
Warning status scale for caution states and alerts.
Error status scale for critical and destructive states.
Informational status scale for neutral notices and help states.
Quick-access feedback pairs — base colour and light background for each status.
Background surface tokens from the Colour Usage collection — Primary, Secondary, and Tertiary surfaces shown with Light and Dark mode values.
Background surface tokens. Primary for main content areas, Secondary for subtle surface differentiation, Tertiary for recessed or nested surfaces.
Text colour tokens from the Colour Usage collection — Primary, Secondary, Tertiary, White, Black, Grey, and Brand shown with Light and Dark mode values.
Text colour tokens. Primary for body copy, Secondary for supporting text, Tertiary for muted labels, White/Black/Grey for fixed-context text, Brand for branded text elements.
Border tokens from the Colour Usage collection — Primary and Secondary borders shown with Light and Dark mode values.
Border tokens. Primary for prominent dividers and input borders, Secondary for subtle separators and container outlines.
Icon colour tokens from the Colour Usage collection — Primary, Secondary, and Tertiary icon colours shown with Light and Dark mode values.
Icon colour tokens. Primary for prominent icons, Secondary for supporting icons, Tertiary for decorative or disabled icons.
Action colour tokens from the Colour Usage collection — Primary, Hover, Active, and Disabled states shown with Light and Dark mode values.
Action tokens for interactive elements. Primary for default interactive state, Hover for pointer hover, Active for pressed/clicked state, Disabled for inactive elements.
Button colour tokens from the Colour Usage collection — Primary, Secondary, status variants, and gradient endpoints shown with Light and Dark mode values.
Button colour tokens. Primary and Secondary for main button styles, Success/Warning/Error for status buttons, Gradient Start/End for gradient button fills.
Feedback colour tokens from the Colour Usage collection — Success, Warning, Error, and Info with their light background variants shown with Light and Dark mode values.
Feedback tokens for status messaging. Each status has a primary colour for text/icons and a light variant for background fills in alerts and banners.
